# tinydelta conformance vectors: what a decoder must produce for a given
# dictionary, patch and output capacity. Any decoder, in any language,
# can be checked against this file (TestVectors and TestCVectors do it for
# the Go and C decoders).
#
# One vector per line, five or six fields separated by single spaces:
#
#   name capacity dictionary patch result [target]
#
# capacity    largest target the decoder may produce, in bytes (decimal, >= 1)
# dictionary  hex, or - for empty
# patch       hex, or - for empty; a valid patch starts with the version
#             byte, 01 or 02 (format version 2: ADD_DIFF in place of
#             COPY_TARGET; v2-* vectors), or 81 or 82 for a coded patch
#             (coded-* vectors). A decoder built without version 2 must
#             return VERSION for every patch starting with 02, and one
#             built without coded patches for every patch starting with 81
#             or 82.
# result      OK, MALFORMED, TOO_LARGE or VERSION (the version byte is
#             none of 01, 02, 81, 82, or a coded patch's features byte
#             names no table layout or sets a reserved bit)
# target      with OK only: the target, hex, or - for empty
#
# Expected results follow the wire format in README.md, plus one rule it
# leaves open: an instruction is checked against the capacity as soon as
# its length is known, before its operands, so an instruction that is both
# too large and malformed is TOO_LARGE. Generated vectors (gen-*) are real
# encoder output; their target is the encoder's input, not decoder output.
